subject: Contract redline: metrics export escrow + subprocessor scoping for LatAm pilot
messages:
From: Mariana Lopez <mariana.lopez@latamhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T10:15:00Z
Subject: DPA redline for pilot - request

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Procurement and our security team have a few asks before we can spin up the pilot: they want an explicit clause restricting exports of inference metrics (usage/latency traces) to an escrow arrangement and a tighter definition of allowed subprocessors for telemetry. Attached is our suggested redline (track changes).

High level asks: 
- Metrics export only to our contracted analytics provider (avoid third-party analytic aggregates).
- No long-term retention of KV-cache snapshots or token-level logs; 30 day max.
- Subprocessor list must be explicit for the pilot region and any changes require 30-day notice.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept these for an initial 6-month pilot? If not, please flag what needs product/security sign-off.

Best,
Mariana
LatAmHealth — Head of Partnerships

Attachment: DPA_redline_latam_v2.docx (Word redline)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Mariana Lopez <mariana.lopez@latamhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T12:04:00Z
Subject: Fwd: DPA redline for pilot - request

Folks — forwarding the redline from LatAmHealth. They want an escrow-only path for metrics export and a 30-day notice window for subprocessor changes confined to the pilot region. Two asks for product/security:

1) Product: Is there any technical blocker to restricting metrics exports to a single partner and ensuring token-level telemetry is purged after 30 days for the pilot? We have caching/KV snapshots; need guidance on snapshot retention and whether rolling purges can be tied to tenant flags.

2) Security/Legal: Subprocessor visibility and notice — can we expose the exact list and commit to 30-day notice for production changes? Also need to confirm if our telemetry pipeline includes any 3rd-party aggregators (e.g., metrics-lake partners).

Mariana has procurement on the loop. Ideally I want a short internal decision so I can get back to them this week.

Thanks — Logan
Product Lead, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline for pilot - request

Logan — quick read-through below. TL;DR: security is ok to scope a limited exception for a pilot but needs controls and traceability.

Notes:
- Metrics export escrow: acceptable if we can isolate the export pipeline to a named destination and build an allowlist for that tenant. Need a config flag and an audit record proving export destinations.
- Token-level logs: 30-day retention is achievable, but for safety we must ensure Kafka retention + S3 lifecycle policies are aligned and that any developers cannot opt out. We'll need a brief runbook for on-call in case of accidental retention.
- Subprocessor notice: 30-day notice is fine but we cannot commit to never using a new helper subprocessor for infra debugging unless we provide an emergency exception process (internal only) and notify the customer within 48 hours. Legal will want the emergency carveout documented.

Open questions for Product (Karthik):
1) Can we set a tenant-level flag that enforces: (a) export destination allowlist, (b) 30d retention lifecycle for logs/KV snapshots, (c) prevents developers from enabling cross-region telemetry exports?
2) Operational impact: will this require a separate telemetry pipeline per region/tenant for isolation, or can we implement logical filtering at export hop? Estimated effort?

I can draft suggested language for security to propose to Legal, but need Product confirm on feasibility and effort estimate.

-Olga
Sr. Security Engineer

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T15:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline for pilot - request

Thanks for the summary. Product perspective: we can deliver the tenant-level controls but with caveats. Quick rundown: 

- Tenant flag: yes — implementable via config at the routing layer. Will enforce export allowlist and apply a retention policy tag on related telemetry objects.
- KV-snapshots: we currently persist short-term snapshots for warm start; we can add a lifecycle to delete after 30 days but there is engineering risk if a customer restarts long-running sessions older than 30 days. For pilots this is acceptable if we document the limitation and add a migration path.
- Export isolation: logical filtering at the export hop is lower cost (2-3 sprint slices) versus full pipeline duplication (4-6 sprints). For a pilot, recommend logical filtering + strict audit logs.

Effort estimate: 3 sprints to build feature flag + allowlist + retention enforcement with 1 sprint of hardening and audit hooks. QA + Security review add 1 sprint.

If Security can draft the redline language outlining the emergency exception flow, Product can accept the 30-day retention and allowlist approach for the pilot. I can draft the short technical note for Mariana.

-Karthik
Director, Product Engineering

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Mariana Lopez <mariana.lopez@latamhealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-06T16:42:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redline for pilot - request (proposal + next steps)

Mariana — thanks for the patience. Internal update and proposal attached.

Summary of what Redwood can sign for the 6-month pilot: 
- Metrics export limited to the named analytics partner via an allowlist; exports will be gated by a tenant-level flag and logged.
- Token-level logs and KV snapshots will be purged after 30 days; we'll include documented limitations about long-running session restores.
- Subprocessor changes: we commit to a 30-day notice for non-emergency additions. Emergency operational needs will use a documented exception process (Redwood will notify within 48 hours and provide a root-cause follow-up).

Next steps: 
1) Olga will produce security wording for the DPA redline (attached as redline_changes_summary.pdf).
2) I will send a short technical appendix from Product describing the flag, retention behavior, and tradeoffs.
3) Mariana — if this aligns, can you confirm procurement is okay to proceed and we can cut a pilot addendum?

Attachments: redline_changes_summary.pdf, export_schema.csv

Onward — Logan
Product Lead, Partnerships
Redwood Inference
